countries.name: Argentina
countries.headline: Bienes Personales continues with falling rates under Milei's 2024 reform
countries.summary: Argentina's personal assets tax (Bienes Personales) still applies to net wealth above an inflation-indexed minimum. The 2024 reform phases rates down through 2027, and the 1.25% bracket has gone. Taxpayers who complied on time get lower rates. For the 2025 fiscal year, filed in 2026, the general minimum was about ARS 384.7m.

countries.name: Australia
countries.headline: Greens' billionaire wealth tax costed by PBO; no government support
countries.summary: Australia has no wealth tax. For the 2025 election the Greens proposed an annual levy on personal net wealth above A$100m, aimed at the country's roughly 150 billionaires. The Parliamentary Budget Office costed it at about A$50bn over a decade. Labor has not adopted it.

countries.name: Austria
countries.headline: Vice-Chancellor Babler (SPÖ) presses for millionaires' tax; ÖVP and NEOS opposed
countries.summary: Austria abolished its net wealth tax in 1994. SPÖ leader and Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler wants a tax on net wealth above €1m, with a €1.5m allowance for the family home, and the party says it would raise about €5bn a year. Coalition partners ÖVP and NEOS reject it, and no government bill exists.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.headline: Securities-account tax doubled to 0.30%; new 10% capital-gains tax from 2026
countries.summary: Belgium has no net wealth tax. It levies an annual tax on securities accounts with an average value above €1m. A programme law of 30 May 2026 doubled the rate from 0.15% to 0.30% for periods ending from 1 June 2026. A 10% tax on realised capital gains on financial assets also took effect on 1 January 2026.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.headline: Large-fortunes tax survives after a legislative committee rejected Paz's repeal bill
countries.summary: Bolivia's Impuesto a las Grandes Fortunas, created in 2020, remains in force. In November 2025 President Rodrigo Paz announced its repeal along with other taxes, but in February 2026 a Chamber of Deputies committee rejected the abolition bill. The tax authority set a 29 May 2026 deadline for 2025 returns.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.headline: Minimum 10% tax on top incomes in force since 2026; wealth tax still unregulated
countries.summary: Brazil's constitution allows a tax on large fortunes, but it has never been regulated. Law 15,270, signed on 26 November 2025 and in force since 1 January 2026, created a minimum effective income tax rising to 10% on incomes above R$1.2m a year. Brazil co-leads the international push to tax the super-rich with Spain, and an April 2026 International Tax Observatory study estimated a 2% minimum tax could raise about R$30bn a year.

countries.name: Canada
countries.headline: New NDP leader Avi Lewis campaigns on 1–3% wealth tax; Carney government not supportive
countries.summary: Canada has no wealth tax. Avi Lewis, elected federal NDP leader on 29 March 2026, proposes 1% on net wealth above C$10m, 2% above C$50m and 3% above C$100m, which he estimates would raise about C$40bn a year. Commentators note that Prime Minister Carney's government shows no sign of backing higher taxes on the rich.

countries.name: Chile
countries.headline: No wealth tax; Kast government's 2026 plan cuts corporate and inheritance taxes
countries.summary: Chile has no net wealth tax, and earlier proposals for a tax on the super-rich did not pass. President Kast's April 2026 economic reconstruction bill moves the other way: it cuts corporate income tax from 27% to 23% and lowers inheritance tax.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.headline: Permanent wealth tax stands; emergency decree that widened it was struck down in 2026
countries.summary: Since Law 2277 of 2022, Colombia has a permanent wealth tax on net worth of 72,000 UVT or more, at 0.5%–1.5%. After Congress rejected the government's 2026 financing bill in December 2025, an emergency decree lowered the threshold to 40,000 UVT and raised rates. The Constitutional Court suspended the emergency in January 2026 and struck it down in April 2026.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.headline: PM Frederiksen proposed reinstating a wealth tax for March 2026 election, then dropped it
countries.summary: Denmark abolished its net wealth tax in 1997. On 26 February 2026 Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen proposed reinstating one for fewer than 60,000 people and called a snap election. On 1 May 2026 she dropped the plan during coalition talks, citing the lack of a parliamentary majority. Enhedslisten still proposes 1% on fortunes above DKK 35m.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.headline: One-off 2022 pandemic-era wealth contribution expired
countries.summary: Ecuador imposed a temporary contribution on individuals with net wealth of at least US$1m (US$2m for couples) under its 2021 post-pandemic fiscal law, payable for 2022. It was a one-off and has not been renewed.

countries.name: Finland
countries.headline: Wealth tax abolished in 2006; Left Alliance proposes 1% millionaires' tax
countries.summary: Finland abolished its net wealth tax in 2006. The opposition Left Alliance proposes a 1% tax on net assets above €1m, excluding the home, and cites polling that three in four Finns back an extra levy on the richest. The Orpo government has instead cut taxes for top earners.

countries.name: France
countries.headline: Real-estate wealth tax (IFI) plus new holding-company levy; Zucman 2% floor rejected, revived by PS
countries.summary: France replaced its net wealth tax in 2018 with the IFI, which taxes real estate only. The National Assembly rejected the Zucman 2% minimum tax on fortunes above €100m on 31 October 2025. The 2026 finance law, adopted in February 2026, created a tax on luxury non-business assets held in family holding companies. In September 2026 the Socialists' counter-budget for 2027 put the Zucman tax back forward.

countries.name: Germany
countries.headline: Wealth tax suspended since 1997; Left motion in committee, Greens propose billionaire tax
countries.summary: Germany has not levied its wealth tax since 1997. The Left's motion to reinstate it, at 1% above €1m rising to 12% above €1bn, was referred to the Bundestag finance committee in March 2026. In September 2026 the Greens proposed a billionaire tax starting at 2% above €500m. The SPD's January 2026 'FairErben' paper targets inheritance tax instead, and the AfD has moved to abolish the dormant wealth tax law.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.headline: Wealth tax abolished 2006; temporary crisis-era version expired after 2014
countries.summary: Iceland abolished its net wealth tax in 2006 and reintroduced it as a temporary emergency measure after the 2008 financial crisis. That version lapsed after 2014, and there is no current proposal.

countries.name: India
countries.headline: Wealth tax abolished in 2015; campaigners urge a 2–6% levy on ultra-rich
countries.summary: India abolished its wealth tax in the 2015 budget and replaced it with a higher income-tax surcharge on incomes above ₹1 crore. In 2026 civil-society groups (CFA and Tax the Top) called for a 2%–6% wealth tax on about 1,688 individuals worth more than ₹1,000 crore. No government proposal exists.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.headline: Opposition alternative budgets for 2027 include wealth taxes; no government plan
countries.summary: Ireland's wealth tax was short-lived in the 1970s, and the country has none today. Ahead of Budget 2027, opposition parties' alternative budgets include wealth-related levies. People Before Profit proposes 'radical' wealth taxes, and Sinn Féin proposes a 3% solidarity tax on incomes above €100,000. The government has no wealth-tax plans.

countries.name: Italy
countries.headline: IVAFE/IVIE on foreign assets; popular initiative and AVS push wealth tax above €2m–5.4m
countries.summary: Italy taxes foreign financial assets (IVAFE) and foreign property (IVIE) but has no general net wealth tax. In May 2026 a committee filed a popular-initiative bill, '1% Equo', for a progressive tax on wealth above €2m. It needs 50,000 signatures by 15 November 2026. In October 2026 the Greens-Left Alliance (AVS) proposed a tax on net wealth above €5.4m for the 2027 election.

countries.name: Japan
countries.headline: Short-lived post-war net wealth tax (from 1950) was repealed in the early 1950s
countries.summary: Japan introduced a net wealth tax in 1950 as part of the Shoup-mission tax reforms. It was repealed after about three years because of low revenue and enforcement problems. There is no current proposal.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.headline: Calls grow to tax the ultra-rich; no wealth tax in Finance Bill 2026
countries.summary: Kenya has no net wealth tax. A November 2025 Oxfam report found the richest 1% hold 78% of financial wealth, and Oxfam estimates a wealth tax could raise over $1bn a year. In September 2026 experts urged the Ruto government to build asset-tracking systems first. The Finance Bill 2026 focuses on capital gains and corporate measures instead.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.headline: Wealth taxed through income tax via a notional 4% return
countries.summary: Liechtenstein does not levy a separate wealth tax. It multiplies an individual's net wealth by a standard 4% notional return (Sollertrag) and adds the result to taxable income. Real estate, securities and other movable assets are included.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.headline: PT deputy files wealth-tax bill; Sheinbaum open to study but no reform planned
countries.summary: Mexico has no wealth tax. In March 2026 a PT deputy proposed 1.5%–3.5% rates on fortunes above MXN 100m, estimating MXN 40–60bn a year. In April 2026 President Sheinbaum said a tax on large fortunes should be analysed but that no tax-raising reform is currently planned.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.headline: Box 3 deemed-return tax; actual-return law passed lower house, stuck in Senate
countries.summary: The Netherlands taxes savings and investments in Box 3 on a deemed return, with a refund if the actual return was lower, under transitional rules until 2027. On 12 February 2026 the lower house passed the Box 3 Actual Return Act, which would tax actual returns, including some unrealised gains, from 2028. The Senate postponed its vote after a debate on 30 June 2026, and amendments are expected.

countries.name: Norway
countries.headline: Net wealth tax kept; 2027 budget raises allowance to NOK 1.99m, rates unchanged
countries.summary: Norway levies a combined municipal and state net wealth tax of 1.0%, rising to 1.1% above NOK 21.5m. The 2026 budget lifted the basic allowance to NOK 1.9m and made a deferred-payment scheme permanent. The 2027 budget proposal of 7 October 2026 raises the allowance to NOK 1.99m and defers larger changes pending the Tax Commission's report.

countries.name: Peru
countries.headline: No wealth tax; left candidate pitched large-fortunes tax in 2026 race
countries.summary: Peru has no general personal wealth tax, though several bills since 2020 have proposed one. In the 30 March 2026 presidential debate, candidate Ronald Atencio proposed a tax on large fortunes to fund education.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.headline: AIMI surcharge on high-value residential property above €600k
countries.summary: Portugal has no net wealth tax. Its Adicional ao IMI (AIMI) is an annual surcharge on the combined taxable value of residential property, above €600,000 per individual (€1.2m for couples filing jointly). Rates run from 0.7% to 1.5%.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.headline: Finance minister keeps rejecting a wealth tax despite pressure from PBO and opposition parties
countries.summary: South Africa has no net wealth tax. Cabinet reportedly considered one during the 2025 budget impasse, and the Parliamentary Budget Office suggested it could raise about R38bn. Finance Minister Godongwana has repeatedly ruled it out, citing a small, mobile tax base. South Africa hosted the 2025 G20 and co-launched the Seville coalition on taxing the super-rich.

countries.name: Spain
countries.headline: Regional wealth tax plus indefinite 'solidarity' tax on fortunes above €3m; Sumar seeks new levy
countries.summary: Spain has a regional net wealth tax and a national Solidarity Tax on Large Fortunes (ISGF) for net wealth above €3m, at 1.7%–3.5%, which has been extended indefinitely. Revenue from the ISGF fell sharply after regions such as Madrid reinstated their own wealth tax. In September 2026 Sumar registered a bill in Congress for an extra levy on fortunes above €50m.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.headline: Left bloc won Sept 2026 election; Left Party and Greens want wealth tax, S leadership says no
countries.summary: Sweden abolished its wealth tax in 2007. The Left Party and the Greens want to reinstate it, and S youth and member groups push a billionaire tax, but Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson has said a wealth tax is not party policy. The left-leaning opposition won a narrow majority on 13 September 2026, and government talks are under way.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.headline: Cantonal wealth taxes remain; voters rejected JUSO 50% inheritance tax; Vaud voted a 12% tax cut
countries.summary: All cantons levy a net wealth tax, with rates and allowances that vary widely between them. On 30 November 2025 voters rejected, by about 78%, the Young Socialists' initiative for a 50% federal tax on estates above CHF 50m. In September 2026 Vaud voters approved a 12% cut in cantonal income and wealth tax from 2027, and several central cantons are also cutting rates.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.headline: No wealth tax; Nov 2025 budget added 'mansion' council-tax surcharge; Greens push 1–2% levy
countries.summary: The UK has no annual wealth tax. The November 2025 budget introduced a High Value Council Tax surcharge on homes worth £2m or more from April 2028. The Green Party under Zack Polanski proposes 1% a year on assets above £10m and 2% above £1bn, which it says would raise about £15bn a year.

countries.name: United States
countries.headline: California votes Nov 3 on one-time 5% billionaire tax; Warren bill reintroduced
countries.summary: There is no federal wealth tax. In March 2026 Sen. Warren and Reps. Jayapal and Boyle reintroduced the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act: 2% a year above $50m plus a billionaire surcharge. California's Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' net worth, is on the 3 November 2026 ballot, with Gov. Newsom backing a rival measure to cancel it. Washington enacted a 9.9% millionaires' income tax, but its wealth tax bills stalled, and Oregon unions filed a wealth-tax initiative for 2028.

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.headline: Wealth tax applies; unions push 1% surcharge on the richest, government rules it out for now
countries.summary: Uruguay levies a net wealth tax (Impuesto al Patrimonio) on individuals above an indexed minimum, set at UYU 6.653m for 2025. In November 2025 the PIT-CNT union federation proposed a 1% surcharge on about 25,000 people with more than US$1m. President Orsi said he would study it, but the Economy Minister has repeatedly rejected it, and in September 2026 the government ruled out short-term tax changes.

items.title: Oregon unions file 'Financial Assets Tax on Multimillionaires' initiative for 2028 ballot
items.summary: A coalition including teachers' and public-sector unions filed a state wealth-tax initiative to offset federal benefit cuts and cut taxes for low earners.

items.title: Norway's 2027 budget proposal lifts wealth-tax allowance to NOK 1.99m, keeps rates
items.summary: Rates and the NOK 21.5m upper-bracket threshold are unchanged; bigger reforms await the Tax Commission's NOU 2026:9.

items.title: Newsom backs Prop 42 to cancel California billionaire tax and bar future wealth taxes
items.summary: Gov. Newsom endorsed a Sergey Brin-funded rival measure that would nullify Prop 40 and ban new taxes on personal property, against parts of his party and labor.

items.title: Five tax measures on California ballot, including billionaire tax Prop 40 and rivals 41 and 42
items.summary: Explainer on the competing measures: if more than one passes, the one with the most votes prevails. Opponents are spending hundreds of millions.

items.title: Italy's Greens-Left Alliance proposes wealth tax on super-rich and tax cuts for 98%
items.summary: AVS's election plan would tax net wealth above €5.4m and challenges Schlein and Conte to back it.

items.title: Irish opposition alternative budgets propose wealth and windfall taxes for 2027
items.summary: Sinn Féin and other parties set out levies on high earners, banks and wealth ahead of Budget 2027.

items.title: New data put Uruguay's top 1% at about 40% of wealth, reviving the tax-the-rich debate
items.summary: A wealth-distribution indicator reignited calls for the PIT-CNT surcharge; the government has ruled out short-term tax changes.

items.title: German Greens propose tax on fortunes above €500m starting at 2%
items.summary: The party says the levy would hit a few hundred people and raise about €20bn a year.

items.title: Vaud voters approve 12% cut in cantonal income and wealth tax
items.summary: Just over 53% backed the business-led initiative; the canton estimates an annual revenue loss of about CHF 272m from 2027.

items.title: Sumar registers bill for new tax on fortunes above €50m in Spanish Congress
items.summary: The proposal targets only the very largest estates and would change the tax treatment of business assets used to cut wealth-tax bills.

items.title: Sweden's left bloc wins narrow majority, with wealth-tax supporters among its parties
items.summary: The Left Party and the Greens back a wealth tax, while Social Democrat leader Andersson has rejected one.

items.title: French Socialists' 2027 counter-budget revives Zucman 2% minimum tax on fortunes over €100m
items.summary: The PS plan puts €39.5bn of new revenue, with the Zucman tax its centrepiece at an estimated €15bn; it is non-binding.

items.title: Calls grow for Kenya to tax wealth of the ultra-rich
items.summary: Experts urge building asset-tracking systems before adopting a net wealth tax.

items.title: UN tax convention talks close fifth session with focus on high-net-worth individuals
items.summary: New York negotiations advanced the framework convention and early protocols; next session is in Nairobi in Nov-Dec 2026.

items.title: South Africa's finance minister again rules out a wealth tax
items.summary: Godongwana said income tax raises far more at lower administrative cost than a levy on the wealthiest.

items.title: Dutch Senate delays vote on Box 3 actual-return tax
items.summary: After a plenary debate, the upper house paused the bill while the government considers softening measures.

items.title: Newsom proposes national billionaires' minimum tax while opposing California's one-time levy
items.summary: The California governor called for a federal minimum tax on people worth over $100m and curbs on tax-free borrowing against stock.

items.title: California one-time 5% billionaire tax qualifies for the November 2026 ballot
items.summary: The Secretary of State confirmed enough valid signatures; the measure taxes net worth of billionaires resident on 1 January 2026, payable over five years.

items.title: Belgium doubles securities-account tax to 0.30% on accounts above €1m
items.summary: The programme law applies the higher rate to reference periods ending from 1 June 2026.

items.title: Popular-initiative bill for Italian wealth tax above €2m launches signature drive
items.summary: The '1% Equo' committee also seeks higher inheritance tax; it needs 50,000 signatures by 15 November 2026.

items.title: Austria's SPÖ and unions renew call for millionaires' tax amid budget deficit
items.summary: Vice-Chancellor Babler's model would tax net wealth above €1m; coalition partners oppose it.

items.title: Danish PM Frederiksen drops wealth tax to ease government talks
items.summary: She said there was no parliamentary majority for the levy proposed before the March election.

items.title: Bundestag debates AfD motion to repeal dormant wealth tax law
items.summary: The motion to abolish the Vermögensteuergesetz was referred to committees.

items.title: Chile's Kast sends tax package cutting corporate and inheritance taxes
items.summary: The reconstruction bill lowers the corporate rate from 27% to 23% and eases inheritance tax; critics say it favours the richest.

items.title: Spain and Brazil agree MoU to coordinate taxation of the super-rich at Barcelona meeting
items.summary: Finance ministers met during the democracy summit in Barcelona, where Gabriel Zucman presented his minimum-tax proposal.

items.title: Sánchez and Lula rally progressive leaders in Barcelona; taxing the super-rich on agenda
items.summary: The 'In Defense of Democracy' gathering followed the first Spain-Brazil summit.

items.title: Study estimates a 2% minimum tax on large Brazilian fortunes could raise R$30bn a year
items.summary: International Tax Observatory work, prefaced by the Finance Ministry, targets about 1,430 people worth over R$500m.

items.title: Sheinbaum says a tax on large fortunes should be analysed, but no reform is planned
items.summary: The Mexican president defended the progressive income tax and opened the door to future study.

items.title: Colombia's Constitutional Court strikes down Petro's economic emergency
items.summary: The ruling knocked down the emergency under which the wealth-tax threshold had been cut and rates raised by decree.

items.title: Indian report urges 2%–6% wealth tax on 1,688 ultra-rich individuals
items.summary: The Wealth Tracker India 2026 by CFA and Tax the Top says the tax could raise ₹10 lakh crore a year.

items.title: Washington enacts 9.9% 'millionaires' tax' on income over $1m; wealth tax bills stall
items.summary: SB 6346 takes effect in 2028. Separate bills for a tax on financial intangible assets stayed in committee when the 2026 session ended.

items.title: Peruvian presidential candidate proposes tax on large fortunes in debate
items.summary: Ronald Atencio pitched a wealth tax with other measures to fund education.

items.title: Avi Lewis wins NDP leadership on platform including wealth tax on richest 1%
items.summary: Lewis estimates his wealth tax would raise about C$40bn a year.

items.title: Warren, Jayapal and Boyle reintroduce Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act with 45+ lawmakers
items.summary: The bill would levy 2% a year on net worth over $50m plus a surcharge on billionaires; Saez and Zucman score it at about $6.2tn over ten years.

items.title: Argentina's personal assets tax: higher minimums and lower rates for 2026 filings
items.summary: Thresholds were indexed about 31% for inflation and the top 1.25% bracket disappears as rates step down toward 2027.

items.title: Left Party motion to reinstate German wealth tax sent to finance committee
items.summary: The motion proposes 1% above €1m rising to 5% at €50m and 12% above €1bn.

items.title: Mexican PT deputy proposes 1.5%–3.5% wealth tax on fortunes above MXN 100m
items.summary: The initiative aims to raise MXN 40–60bn a year to reduce poverty.

items.title: Danish PM proposes reinstating wealth tax as she calls snap election
items.summary: Frederiksen's plan, expected to raise about $1bn, would hit fewer than 60,000 people.

items.title: France's 2026 finance law creates tax on luxury assets held in family holding companies
items.summary: Adopted via Article 49.3 on 2 February and largely upheld by the Constitutional Council, the levy targets non-business assets in holdings worth over €5m.

items.title: Dutch lower house passes Box 3 reform taxing actual investment returns from 2028
items.summary: The bill replaces deemed returns on savings and investments with taxation of real returns.

items.title: Bolivian deputies' committee rejects bill to abolish large-fortunes tax
items.summary: The planning committee kept the wealth tax while approving repeal of the financial transactions tax.

items.title: Colombian court provisionally suspends emergency decree and its new taxes
items.summary: A 6-2 vote suspended the emergency, including the decree widening the wealth tax to holdings above 40,000 UVT.

items.title: Oxfam: billionaire wealth hit record $18.3tn in 2025, calls for taxes on extreme wealth
items.summary: Released as Davos opened, the 'Resisting the Rule of the Rich' report urges higher taxes on the richest.

items.title: SPD unveils 'FairErben' inheritance tax concept with €1m lifetime allowance
items.summary: The paper would sharply limit business-asset exemptions; it is a discussion concept, not a bill.

items.title: Belgium introduces 10% tax on capital gains from financial assets
items.summary: Gains from 1 January 2026 are taxed at 10% above an indexed €10,000 annual exemption.

items.title: Colombian Congress sinks Petro's 2026 financing tax reform
items.summary: Economic committees voted 9-4 against the bill, prompting the government to turn to emergency decrees.

items.title: Norway's 2026 budget raises wealth-tax allowance and makes deferral scheme permanent
items.summary: The basic allowance rose from NOK 1.76m to NOK 1.9m and the low-valuation limit for homes rose to NOK 14m.

items.title: Wealth tax off the table for South Africa, says Treasury
items.summary: The finance minister reiterated that the current system raises and redistributes revenue more effectively.

items.title: Swiss voters reject JUSO initiative for 50% tax on inheritances over CHF 50m
items.summary: About 78% voted no and no canton approved it; proceeds would have funded climate measures.

items.title: Oxfam: richest 1% hold 78% of Kenya's financial wealth
items.summary: The report urges progressive taxation of wealth and ring-fenced spending on health and education.

items.title: UK budget adds surcharge on homes worth £2m+ instead of a wealth tax
items.summary: The High Value Council Tax charge starts in April 2028 alongside higher dividend and property income tax rates.

items.title: Lula signs law creating minimum 10% tax on Brazil's top incomes
items.summary: Law 15,270 exempts earnings up to R$5,000 a month and imposes a minimum rate on incomes above R$600k, reaching 10% above R$1.2m, from 2026.

items.title: Bolivian President Paz moves to scrap large-fortunes tax to attract investment
items.summary: Paz announced repeal of four taxes, arguing the 2020 wealth tax drove investment abroad.

items.title: G20 Johannesburg summit ends without progress on taxing the super-rich, says Greenpeace
items.summary: Advocates praised South Africa's leadership but said no new commitments followed the 2024 Rio pledge.

items.title: UN tax convention talks resume in Nairobi with focus on high-net-worth individuals
items.summary: The third negotiating session debated an article on taxing wealthy individuals alongside allocation of taxing rights.

items.title: Uruguayan unions propose 1% surcharge on wealth of the richest 1%
items.summary: The PIT-CNT plan would hit about 25,000 people with over US$1m and fund households with children.

items.title: French National Assembly rejects Zucman tax and Socialist alternative in 2026 budget debate
items.summary: Lawmakers voted down the 2% levy on wealth above €100m and a 3% levy above €10m; the government offered a holding-company tax instead.

items.title: Union-backed one-time billionaire tax initiative filed in California
items.summary: SEIU-UHW's proposal would impose a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' wealth to fund health care after federal cuts.

items.title: Spain, Brazil and South Africa launch coalition to tax the super-rich at FfD4 in Seville
items.summary: The Sevilla Platform for Action initiative invites more countries to join; Oxfam and Greenpeace welcomed it.
